children: Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 rise 0.7 per cent and 0.9 per cent, respectively

Indian equity markets recovered on 23 September, with the Nifty crossing the 23,400-mark as broad-based buying in metals, realty, financials and consumer stocks outweighed continued weakness in information technology (IT) shares.
The Sensex gained 299.17 points, or 0.40 per cent, to close at 74,828.25, while the Nifty rose 117.80 points, or 0.50 per cent, to 23,446.80.
The broader market also recovered from two consecutive sessions of losses, with the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 rising 0.7 per cent and 0.9 per cent, respectively.

Metal stocks led the sectoral recovery, with the Nifty Metal index climbing 2.4 per cent. Telecom, public sector banks, realty and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) stocks also gained more than 1 per cent each. The Nifty IT index fell 0.8 per cent, while media stocks declined 0.5 per cent.

Sentiment was supported by the decline in crude oil prices, which extended their losing streak to six sessions. The fall in oil prices offered some relief to domestic equities amid mixed global cues, although persistent selling in IT stocks limited the market's gains.

“Geopolitical developments at the UN General Assembly kept a risk premium embedded in oil prices, which weighed on the INR amid a firmer U.S. dollar. However, a stronger-than-expected September flash PMI reinforced confidence in the resilience of economic activity, indicating that growth remains intact without a corresponding build-up in inflationary pressures,” said Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments.
Tata Steel, Bajaj Finance, Hindalco Industries, JSW Steel and Apollo Hospitals were among the biggest Nifty gainers.
Coal India, HCL Technologies, Titan Company, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Infosys were among the key laggards.

Among individual stocks, Prime Focus declined more than 6 per cent after Brahma AI raised USD 150 million through an equity issuance. Optiemus Infracom, meanwhile, surged 17 per cent, with around 15.85 lakh shares changing hands in block deals.
Financial stocks also found support after UBS upgraded Bajaj Finance to Neutral and L&T Finance to Buy. The two stocks gained around 2-3 per cent.
Texmaco Infrastructure rose 7 per cent after around 1.28 crore shares changed hands in a block deal. Persistent Systems fell 2.5 per cent after it acquired a 61.15 per cent stake in Nagarro SE.

Elsewhere, Allcargo Terminals gained 8 per cent after reporting a 6 per cent rise in August volumes. 360 ONE WAM advanced more than 3 per cent after Aashish Agarwal was appointed chief executive officer.
